questions.stem: The chief difference between having a constitution and practising constitutionalism is that constitutionalism requires

options.text: that the constitution be written in a single document
that those in power actually submit to the limits the constitution imposes
that the constitution be very long and detailed
that the constitution be approved in a national referendum

questions.explanation: Nearly every state, including military regimes, has some constitutional document. Constitutionalism is the practice of governing within those limits and being effectively checked when they are exceeded. Without enforcement, the document is only paper.

distractorRationale.a: Britain has no codified document yet a long tradition of constitutionalism
distractorRationale.c: Length is irrelevant; a detailed constitution that is ignored delivers no constitutionalism
distractorRationale.d: How a constitution is adopted says nothing about whether rulers later obey it

questions.stem: The three principles of the rule of law are traditionally associated with

options.text: Baron de Montesquieu
A. V. Dicey
John Locke
Jean-Jacques Rousseau

questions.explanation: Dicey set out the classic three principles: absence of arbitrary power, equality before the law, and rights secured through decisions of the ordinary courts. Each of the other thinkers is famous for a different doctrine.

distractorRationale.a: Montesquieu is associated with the separation of powers, not the rule of law
distractorRationale.c: Locke is remembered for natural rights and government by consent
distractorRationale.d: Rousseau is associated with the general will and popular sovereignty

questions.stem: The fundamental human rights that a Nigerian citizen can enforce in court are contained in

options.text: Chapter II of the 1999 Constitution
Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution
the Second Schedule to the 1999 Constitution
the preamble to the 1999 Constitution

questions.explanation: Chapter IV, sections 33 to 46, holds the justiciable rights — life, dignity, personal liberty, fair hearing, private life, religion, expression, assembly, movement, freedom from discrimination and property. Section 46 gives a citizen alleging a breach direct access to a High Court.

distractorRationale.a: Chapter II holds the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles, which section 6(6)(c) expressly makes non-justiciable
distractorRationale.c: The Second Schedule contains the legislative lists dividing power between the federal and state governments
distractorRationale.d: A preamble states the spirit in which a constitution is adopted and confers no enforceable rights

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, Chapter IV

questions.stem: Which of the following is guaranteed by section 36 of the 1999 Constitution?

options.text: The right to fair hearing
The right to free primary education
The right to a well-paid job
The right to own a firearm

questions.explanation: Section 36 guarantees fair hearing: a person is entitled to be heard by an impartial court within a reasonable time, to be presumed innocent, to know the charge, and to defend themselves in person or through a lawyer of their choice.

distractorRationale.b: Free education is a Chapter II directive principle under section 18, and section 6(6)(c) makes it non-justiciable
distractorRationale.c: Suitable employment is likewise a Chapter II objective and cannot be enforced in court
distractorRationale.d: The Constitution grants no right to own a firearm; that is a matter for ordinary firearms legislation

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, sections 18 and 36

questions.stem: Which THREE of the following limit the operation of the rule of law in Nigeria?

options.text: The immunity granted to the President and state Governors while in office
Poverty and the high cost of litigation, which keep the courts out of reach
The right of appeal to a higher court
Delegated legislation and wide discretionary powers given to officials
The presumption that an accused person is innocent until proved guilty

questions.explanation: Immunity under section 308 places certain office holders temporarily beyond the reach of proceedings, undermining equality before the law. Poverty makes the courts inaccessible in practice. Wide discretion allows officials to act on their own judgement rather than on settled rules, which is the arbitrary power Dicey warned against.

distractorRationale.c: The right of appeal supports the rule of law by allowing errors to be corrected
distractorRationale.e: The presumption of innocence is a pillar of the rule of law, not a limitation on it

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, section 308

questions.stem: Dicey's principle of equality before the law means that

options.text: every citizen must earn the same income
public officials are subject to the same law and the same courts as ordinary citizens
the law must treat every offence with the same punishment
all citizens must be given equal seats in the legislature

questions.explanation: Equality before the law is about legal, not economic or political, equality. No one is above the law by reason of rank or office, and there is no separate system of courts for officials accused of wrongdoing.

distractorRationale.a: Equal income is a matter of economic policy, not of the rule of law
distractorRationale.c: Punishment is properly graded to the seriousness of the offence; equality concerns who the law applies to
distractorRationale.d: Legislative representation is a question of electoral design, not of equality before the law

questions.stem: The fundamental rights guaranteed in Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution are absolute and can never be restricted.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Section 45 allows laws reasonably justifiable in a democratic society to restrict certain rights in the interest of defence, public safety, public order, public morality or public health, or to protect the rights of others. Section 305 also permits derogation during a declared state of emergency.

distractorRationale.a: Calling the rights fundamental describes their importance, not an immunity from every possible limitation

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, sections 45 and 305

questions.stem: Explain four conditions necessary for constitutionalism to thrive in a country.
markingGuide: An independent judiciary, able to declare acts of the executive or legislature unconstitutional without fear of removal or of losing its funding (2 marks)
Separation of powers with real checks and balances, so that no single organ can act without restraint from the others (2 marks)
Guaranteed and enforceable fundamental human rights, with an accessible remedy such as that provided by section 46 of the 1999 Constitution (2 marks)
Regular, free and fair elections, so that rulers who abuse power can be removed peacefully by the electorate (2 marks)
Any one of: a free press and active civil society exposing abuse; accountability and transparency in public finance; a politically literate citizenry willing to defend the constitution (2 marks)
questions.explanation: Each condition should be explained in terms of the check it supplies rather than merely named. The strongest answers point out that these conditions reinforce one another: an independent judiciary is worthless if its orders are disobeyed, and elections are meaningless if the press cannot report on the government's record.
